reasons: In-scope and correctly directed: Section 2.1 makes Customer unconditionally liable for USD 2,000,000/year 'on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights', i.e. payment for Services not consumed and a minimum amount surviving termination — squarely within the rule's detection of 'minimum fees on termination' / penalties payable by Customer. Only Customer-payable exposure is addressed; Customer-facing remedies (10.2, 19.4, 27.3) are untouched.

Deviation status is justified against the preferred position ('No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer'), and the internal conflict with Section 12.3 (no minimum-volume commitment) reinforces rather than substitutes for the finding.

Redline is valid, self-contained, and operative: it converts the volume figure to a non-binding forecast and expressly negates shortfall, penalty and early-termination charges while preserving reduction/non-renewal/termination rights that the original clause stripped. Consistent with redline guidance ('Delete the Customer-payable LD').

The failed minimality check (0.895 changed characters) is not disqualifying here because the rule prescribes deletion of the offending obligation; any compliant edit to a one-sentence take-or-pay covenant necessarily rewrites nearly the whole paragraph, and the replacement adds no unrelated protections.

Comment meets tone and content requirements: concise, first-person plural, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position, flags the 12.3 conflict, and offers the sanctioned fallback (early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees).

Minor, non-fatal notes for the negotiator: (i) the edit removes the committed-spend bargain entirely rather than only its penal element — a narrower alternative is to keep the volume figure but strike 'on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights' and add the no-shortfall sentence, which may better preserve any volume-based pricing discount; (ii) the phrase 'in this Agreement or an Order Form' reaches beyond the cited paragraph, which is defensible as anti-circumvention but should be confirmed against existing Order Form terms.
